title: Runtime lifecycle provenance and course corrections
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the end-to-end runtime lifecycle used by Redwood’s serving runtime, the provenance signals we capture at each stage, and a set of operational "course-corrections" (automatic and manual) for common regressions. It bridges architecture, kernel scheduling policy, profiling playbooks, benchmark requirements, release highlights, known issues, and runbook recipes into a single operational reference.

Audience: runtime engineers, SREs, performance owners, and release managers.

Goals
- Provide a clear, reproducible model of request flow and the observable signals at each lifecycle stage.
- Standardize kernel scheduling guardrails and a compact policy language for predictable latency/cost tradeoffs.
- Define profiling and benchmarking protocols for validating changes.
- Offer concrete runbooks and corrective actions for production incidents.

Scope
Applies to all hosted and dedicated runtime clusters managed by Redwood (hosted-api, dedicated pools, private-runtime bundles). Does NOT cover customer-side inference code or SDKs.

Key terminology
- Request timeline: sequence from ingress -> classification -> routing -> scheduling -> execute -> emit -> postprocess.
- Execution unit: indivisible actor that maps to a kernel dispatch on a GPU (may span multiple kernels for long-decoder steps).
- Kernel-credit: accounting unit used by the scheduler to ensure fairness and protect SLOs.
- Provenance event: structured telemetry record emitted at well-known checkpoints with deterministic keys (trace_id, request_class, model_variant, kernel_shard, kv_hit, latency_ms, cost_token_units).

1) Runtime architecture summary
High-level flow (textual diagram):
- INGRESS -> CLASSIFIER -> ROUTER -> SCHEDULER -> KERNEL-EXEC -> KV-CACHE -> EMIT -> METRICS/LOGS/AUDIT-STORE

Responsibilities by component (short):
- Ingress: rate-limit, authz, initial sampling. Emits ingress_provenance.
- Classifier: inspects payload size, prompt shape, and model hints; sets request_class tag.
- Router: maps request_class -> pool (region, GPU family, capacity tier). Can rewrite model_variant for cost fallback.
- Scheduler: performs priority selection, slotting, batching, and kernel credit deduction.
- Kernel-exec: runs optimized kernels on device; emits kernel_profiling trace for each dispatch.
- KV-cache: prefix and KV hits; observable for hit-rate, warm-up slope, and eviction churn.
- Emit: streaming vs non-streaming paths with different durability and backpressure modes.

Provenance signals (minimum set captured at each checkpoint)
- ingress_provenance: {trace_id, timestamp, api_key_hash, route_id, request_size_tokens}  // emitted at ingress
- classification_provenance: {trace_id, request_class, expected_seq_len, model_hint}  // classifier output
- routing_provenance: {trace_id, pool_id, model_variant, fallback_reason?}  // selected pool/variant
- scheduling_provenance: {trace_id, ticket_id, priority_band, credit_before, credit_after, slot_count}  // before dispatch
- kernel_profiling: {trace_id, kernel_id, dispatch_index, duration_us, occupancy_pct, cuda_stream, mem_bytes}  // per dispatch
- kv_provenance: {trace_id, shard_id, hit_bool, warmup_hint}  // cache interaction
- emit_provenance: {trace_id, final_latency_ms, http_status, shard_route}  // end of request

All provenance events include service_version and git_commit to make traces usable for regression attribution.

2) Kernel scheduling policy overview
We enforce a compact, declarative scheduling policy used by the slot allocator and kernel admission controller. Policies are evaluated per-pool and are versioned.

Policy language (example YAML snippet)
```
policy_version: 2
priority_bands:
  - name: realtime
    min_tokens: 0
    max_tokens: 2048
    preemption: true
    kernel_credit_rate: 10
  - name: interactive
    min_tokens: 2049
    max_tokens: 8192
    preemption: false
    kernel_credit_rate: 5
  - name: batch
    min_tokens: 8193
    max_tokens: 131072
    preemption: false
    kernel_credit_rate: 2
slot_allocation:
  algorithm: proportional_fair
  bias_configs:
    realtime: 0.6
    interactive: 0.3
    batch: 0.1
backpressure:
  request_queue_max_ms: 300
  sample_drop_percent: 0.05
```
Notes on fields:
- kernel_credit_rate: credits per second allocated to a band. Higher rate -> lower expected latency at cost of throughput fairness.
- preemption: whether a higher band can preempt active lower-band executions (cooperative preemption). Use sparingly for GPU kernels that support safe preemption.

Scheduling invariants (must hold across all runtime versions)
- Band isolation: observed 99.9th percentile latency of band X must not exceed baseline*(1 + band_sla_tolerance).
- Credit conservation: sum(kernel_credit_rate * weight) across bands must be <= pool_max_credits.
- Safe preemption: preemption may only be enabled when runtime_can_checkpoint==true for the model_variant.

3) Profiling playbook (for runtime regressions)
When a regression is detected (latency or error-rate bump), follow this triage sequence:
1) Verify: confirm regression in Canary and in production rollup dashboards (last 1h and 24h).
2) Isolate: use trace_id sampling to find top 10 slow traces. Correlate with git_commit and model_variant.
3) Surface provenance: extract full provenance event chain for sample traces (ingress -> kernel_profiling -> kv_provenance -> emit).
4) Microprofile: enable high-fidelity kernel_profiling for affected pool (5–10% sample) for 30 minutes.
5) Kernel diff: compare kernel dispatch duration distribution against baseline using the kernel-diff tool.
6) Act: apply course-correction (see table below).

Course-corrections (ordered by risk)
- Auto: increase slot_allocation bias for realtime band by +10% for 5 minutes (low risk).
- Low-friction: temporarily disable batch band preemption in pool (reduces tail spikes).
- Medium: roll forward small kernel patch with autotest gated (requires rolling canary).
- High: rollback last kernel/driver change and trigger capacity rebootstrap (requires SRE approval).

Instrumentation checklist (profiling)
- Ensure all provenance events include service_version and git_commit.
- Kernel traces must include occupancy_pct and memory_high_watermark.
- KV-cache metrics: per-shard hit_rate, insert_rate, eviction_rate.
- Tracing correlation: link all events using trace_id and ticket_id.

CLI commands (examples)
- Collect a 10-minute sample from pool "g-pool-a":
  rpctl collect --pool g-pool-a --duration 600 --sample-rate 0.05 --out /tmp/pool-sample.tar.gz
- Run kernel diff between sample and baseline:
  kernel-diff --baseline /artifacts/baseline-2026-01 --sample /tmp/pool-sample.tar.gz --out /tmp/diff-report.html

4) Benchmarking suite and acceptance protocol
Benchmark goals: ensure PRs that touch scheduler, batching, KV cache, or kernel selection provide evidence that:
- median and p95 latency regressions are < 3% for standard short-seq workloads, and < 7% for long-seq workloads.
- per-token cost change is within expected error margins (< 5% for non-quantizing changes).

Standard benchmark profiles (text table):
| profile_name | seq_len_p50 | seq_len_p95 | concurrency | mix | purpose |
| short_interactive | 64 | 256 | 200 | 90% realtime, 10% interactive | latency SLO smoke test |
| long_batch | 4096 | 8192 | 50 | 100% batch | throughput/cost evaluation |
| mixed_multi_variant | 32 | 2048 | 400 | 60% realtime, 30% interactive, 10% batch | stress and fairness |

Acceptance protocol for runtime changes:
1) Run local microbenchmarks and upload artifacts.
2) Execute full benchmark suite against canary pool (3 noisy runs, median result used).
3) If p95 regressions exceed thresholds, add a mitigation plan or revert.
4) For kernel changes, include kernel-diff and list of affected dispatches.

5) Release notes (excerpt)
v2026.01 (2026-01-20)
- Introduced deterministic provenance keys across all runtime components (improves triage fidelity).
- New priority_band "interactive" for mixed workloads and proportional_fair slot allocation.
- Kernel credit accounting added to scheduler; default pool configs updated with conservative credit limits.
- Fixed regression: kv-cache eviction hot-loop causing 2–4x insert latency on GPU shard.

6) Known issues (current catalog)
- nvlink_fanout_degradation_2026_02: intermittent nvlink peer hang under extreme GPU fragmentation. Workaround: drain node and drain-replace until compaction job completes. (workaround documented in eng-infra runbook).
- small_shard_tail_growth: small-model shards occasionally observe 15–30ms tail growth during mixed traffic. Mitigation: increase prefill batch size or route small-model traffic to dedicated micro-pool.
- driver-compat-451: certain driver patches reduce cooperative-preemption throughput; policy preemption default is disabled for pools with driver < 452.

7) Runbooks (practical recipes)
A) Latency tail spike triage (15 minute playbook)
1) Check dashboard: locate affected pool(s) and confirm increased p99 latency over baseline.
2) Run rpctl collect on top-5 nodes for 10 minutes (sample_rate 0.05).
3) Pull kernel-diff report and examine top 3 kernels by median delta.
4) If kernel delta > 30% and recent kernel roll happened in last 24h: rollback kernel rollout.
5) If KV hit_rate < 30% and warmup slope > 0.2s/1000req: increase kv-cache prefetch factor for affected shard.
6) Monitor for 30m. If unresolved, engage oncall (pager) and open incident.

B) Cache thrash recovery (30 minute playbook)
1) Identify shard eviction_rate and ownership churn.
2) If eviction_rate > 200/s for 5 minutes, enable temporary conservative eviction_policy: target_utilization -= 15%.
3) Kick an async compaction job to defragment allocations on node.
4) If compaction fails on > 2 nodes, schedule rolling-restart with drained traffic.

8) Team wiki notes and ownership
- Owning teams and rotations:
  - runtime-core: primary for scheduler, kernel credits, and provenance schema. (owner: runtime-core@redwood.dev)
  - infra-gpu: handles host-level NVLink and driver rollout; pager for host hangs. (owner: infra-gpu@redwood.dev)
  - observability: manages trace ingestion, provenance schema, and dashboards. (owner: observability@redwood.dev)

On-call responsibilities: any high-severity regression should notify runtime-core and infra-gpu simultaneously. The runbook author is responsible for ensuring playbooks are executable and kept in sync with tools.

Appendix A — Provenance schema (compact reference)
- field list: trace_id, timestamp_iso, service_version, git_commit, pool_id, model_variant, request_class, seq_len, kernel_shard, kernel_id, dispatch_ms, kv_hit, response_size_tokens, cost_token_units

Appendix B — Quick links
- Kernel diff tool: /internal/tools/kernel-diff
- Slot allocator docs: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/scheduler-policy-language-declarative-profiles-2026
- Benchmarking runner: /internal/benchmarks/runner

If you are making changes that touch scheduling, kernel selection, KV-cache allocation, or preemption flags, update this document and attach benchmark artifacts to the PR.

End of document
